name: Dawn

landing.label: Occator Crater (Cerealia Facula), Dwarf Planet Ceres

terrain.note: Perpetual stable gravitational orbit around Ceres, overflying ancient ice-rich cryovolcanic calderas

keyDiscovery: First probe to orbit two separate extraterrestrial destinations (Vesta and Ceres), discovering cryomagma, water ice reservoirs, and luminous sodium carbonate salt deposits.
missionLegacy: Exemplified deep-space ion propulsion, traveling billions of kilometers with just 425 kg of xenon propellant, remaining in silent quarantine orbit around Ceres for centuries.

objects.name: Dawn Spacecraft Core Bus
objects.description: Hexagonal graphite composite spacecraft bus housing hydrazine reaction control thrusters, four reaction wheels, and star trackers.
objects.scienceDiscovery: Successfully performed orbital insertion, spiraling descent, orbital escape, and second insertion between Vesta and Ceres.
objects.legacy: The only spacecraft ever to orbit two extraterrestrial bodies.
objects.firstPerson: I am Dawn. I bridged the gulf between rocky giant protoplanet Vesta and ice dwarf Ceres, now silent in my eternal orbit.

objects.name: NSTAR Xenon Ion Thruster Trio
objects.description: Three 30-centimeter gridded electrostatic xenon ion thrusters firing turquoise-glowing hyper-efficient plasma jets with 3,100 s specific impulse.
objects.scienceDiscovery: Logged 51,385 hours of active ion thrusting, achieving a record-shattering velocity change of 11.5 km/s.
objects.legacy: Pioneered electric ion propulsion as a routine interplanetary propulsion technology.
objects.firstPerson: I whispered through the blackness of deep space on glowing blue beams of xenon ions, gently accelerating month after month.

objects.name: 19.7-Meter UltraFlex Solar Arrays
objects.description: Two massive 8.3 x 2.3 m deployable solar wings spanning 19.7 meters tip-to-tip, generating 10,000 W at Earth and 1,300 W in the asteroid belt.
objects.scienceDiscovery: Powered deep-space ion engines at 3 AU from the Sun using advanced high-efficiency triple-junction solar cells.
objects.legacy: Largest solar arrays flown on an interplanetary robotic science mission at the time.
objects.firstPerson: My giant wings caught the faint rays of the distant Sun, gathering every precious photon to feed my ion engines.

objects.name: DLR Framing Cameras (FC)
objects.description: Twin redundant refractive telephoto framing cameras built by the German Aerospace Center (DLR) with 1024x1024 CCD arrays.
objects.scienceDiscovery: Captured over 100,000 high-resolution images, charting Rheasilvia crater's central peak (one of the tallest mountains in the Solar System).
objects.legacy: Delivered the first comprehensive geological atlases of Vesta and Ceres.
objects.firstPerson: My lenses looked down upon giant impact basins and glowing salt domes, revealing worlds once seen only as fuzzy dots of light.

objects.name: Visible & Infrared Spectrometer (VIR)
objects.description: Imaging spectrometer provided by the Italian Space Agency (ASI) covering 0.25 to 5.0 micrometers to map surface mineralogy.
objects.scienceDiscovery: Identified ammoniated phyllosilicates across Ceres, proving Ceres originated in the outer Solar System before migrating inwards.
objects.legacy: Confirmed the chemical fingerprint of dwarf planets and their connections to Kuiper Belt objects.
objects.firstPerson: I analyzed the colors of reflected infrared light to identify water ice, clays, and salt minerals across dwarf planet Ceres.

objects.name: Cerealia Facula Salt Caldera
objects.description: Luminous sodium carbonate hydrothermal salt deposits inside Occator Crater, formed by brine erupting from a subterranean slush reservoir.
objects.scienceDiscovery: Proved Ceres is a geologically active relic ocean world with lingering subsurface brine pockets and cryovolcanic activity.
objects.legacy: Redefined dwarf planets as living geochemical laboratories rather than frozen dead rocks.
objects.firstPerson: We are the luminous salt crowns of Occator Crater, shimmering against dark asteroid ground like celestial beacons.
